defects.claim_says: The single clause, defined to include the naming sentence ('This reservation shall be known as the Minnewastena Migratory Waterfowl Refuge'), ended on 1958-08-05; the only later event is Reorganization Plan No. II; 'No earlier named instrument ... was found'.
defects.source_says: Proclamation No. 2416, 'Changing the Names of Certain Federal Wildlife Refuges', signed July 25, 1940, filed July 27, 1940, 5 FR 2677-2680 (Federal Register of July 30, 1940), held in the FR text layer jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_8494.txt (sha256 87e6c363552ebc78ddc3b93a269adfe3752ef2d318a06f44831141791d006bb8; also EO_8496.txt): 'do proclaim that the names of the Federal wildlife refuges listed below are hereby changed as indicated', with the old-name column listing 'Minnewastena Migratory Waterfowl Refuge' and the new-name column 'Minnewastena National Wildlife Refuge'. A held presidential instrument that names this refuge changed the name this order prescribed on July 25, 1940, eighteen years before PLO 1704. The claim omits this later event and states that the naming command ended in 1958; the searches were by order number only and could not find a renaming by refuge name.

defects.claim_says: The single clause, which includes the naming sentence ('This reservation shall be known as the Pioneer Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge'), ended on 1958-08-05 by Public Land Order 1704. The only later event is Reorganization Plan No. II, and no earlier named instrument was found.
defects.source_says: Proclamation No. 2416, 'Changing the Names of Certain Federal Wildlife Refuges', was signed July 25, 1940, filed July 27, 1940, and printed at 5 FR 2677-2680 (Federal Register of July 30, 1940). Its held FR text layer is jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_8494.txt (sha256 87e6c363552ebc78ddc3b93a269adfe3752ef2d318a06f44831141791d006bb8; also EO_8496.txt). It says: 'do proclaim that the names of the Federal wildlife refuges listed below are hereby changed as indicated'. The old-name column lists 'Pioneer Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge' and the new-name column lists 'Pioneer Lake National Wildlife Refuge'. This held presidential act names the refuge and replaced the order's naming command 18 years before PLO 1704. The claim omits it.

defects.claim_says: registered Federal Register original (10 FR, issue of 1945-04-27 ...)
defects.source_says: The cited original is the issue of Tuesday, April 17, 1945 (URL FR-1945-04-17; 10 FR 4057; filed Apr. 14, 1945). The 'April 27' reading comes from the garbled OCR masthead ('.Apri/ 27, 2025'); April 27, 1945 was a Friday. The rationale contradicts the claim's own original_representation.

defects.claim_says: no earlier revoking or superseding instrument; the only earlier event is the Executive Order 10415 amendment
defects.source_says: Executive Order 10804, signed February 12, 1959 (24 FR 1147, jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_10804.txt), section 2 revokes Executive Order 9721 of May 10, 1946, the order whose paragraph 3(a) this order modified, except for employees serving with an international organization on the date of enactment of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act who do not elect its coverage and for rights and benefits vested before that date

defects.claim_says: paragraph 3(a) of Executive Order 9721 is a separate command which Executive Order 12553 also lists as revoked (implying the parent stood until 1986)
defects.source_says: the parent was revoked in 1959 by Executive Order 10804 subject to a limited saving; by Executive Order 10415 the modified right required service to end on or before December 31, 1953, so whether anything of this order survived the 1959 revocation (through the saving for vested rights) must be analysed before 1986-02-25 can be the first end

defects.claim_says: section 2 of EO 10804 'revokes 9721 and 10103 insofar as they affect employees covered by section 6(a) of the International Atomic Energy Agency Participation Act of 1957' ('an express revocation, but only insofar as the orders affect employees covered by section 6(a)'; 'earlier revoked the order only in part')
defects.field: research_rationale (Ending; Member checks earlier_end_check) and operative_clauses[0].judgment_reason
defects.source_says: EO 10804 section 2 (24 FR 1147) reads 'Executive Order No. 9721 of May 10, 1946; Executive Order No, 10103 of February 1, 1950; and Executive Order No. 10774 of July 25, 1958, insofar as it affects any employee covered by section 6(a) of the International Atomic Energy Agency Participation Act of 1957 ... are revoked except that each shall be considered to remain in effect with respect to any employee ... who does not elect to have coverage ... and for the purposes of any rights and benefits vested'. The singular 'insofar as it affects' qualifier follows the semicolon-separated list and attaches to EO 10774 only. EO 9721 and EO 10103 are revoked generally, subject only to the two saving exceptions; they are not revoked solely as to section 6(a) IAEA employees.
